title: One Live Plan to a Covered Piece under the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans
content:
One covered piece carries at most the number of plans of the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans the plan itself allows, and in practice a piece is covered by one plan at a time. A further protection plan is written against a piece only when no plan already recorded against the same covered item reference stands at quoted, active, inspection overdue or suspended. A plan that has expired, been cancelled, been transferred away or had its allowance consumed no longer occupies the piece, so fresh coverage may then be quoted where the coverage is still offered for that piece.

## How the test is taken

The count is taken against the covered piece, not against the customer: the plans looked at are those recorded against the same covered item reference as the piece being quoted. What the records show governs, and the standing of any plan already on that piece is read from the plan record rather than from what the customer recalls holding. The test is taken before the new quote is written.

## Standings that do and do not occupy the piece

| Standing of a plan already on that covered item reference | Does it bar a further plan being written on the piece |
|---|---|
| quoted | yes |
| active | yes |
| inspection overdue | yes |
| suspended | yes |
| expired | no |
| cancelled | no |
| transferred | no |
| exhausted (the allowance consumed) | no |

## Two readings of the same piece

A piece carries a plan standing at suspended for unpaid premium. No further plan is written against that piece while that standing holds, because a suspended plan still occupies the piece.

The same piece later carries only a plan that closed as cancelled. That plan no longer occupies the piece, so fresh coverage may be quoted on it where the coverage is still offered for that piece.
